---
title: Choosing parameters
description: What n_neighbors, min_dist, metric and the other parameters do, with examples.
jupyter: python3
---

polars-umap uses the same parameter names and defaults as
[umap-learn](https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/parameters.html), so its guidance
applies here too. The defaults are a good start; two parameters are worth exploring.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import altair as alt
import polars as pl
from sklearn.datasets import load_digits

import polars_umap  # noqa: F401

alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows()
X, y = load_digits(return_X_y=True)
digits = pl.DataFrame({"pixels": X, "digit": y})


def grid(param: str, values: list, **fixed) -> alt.Chart:
    frames = [
        digits.umap.fit_transform("pixels", random_state=42, **{param: v}, **fixed)
        .select("digit", "umap_0", "umap_1")
        .with_columns(pl.lit(f"{param} = {v}").alias("panel"))
        for v in values
    ]
    order = [f"{param} = {v}" for v in values]
    return (
        alt.Chart(pl.concat(frames))
        .mark_circle(size=6, opacity=0.5, color="#8d8b86")
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("umap_0", axis=None),
            y=alt.Y("umap_1", axis=None),
            tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("digit:N", title="Digit")],
        )
        .properties(width=118, height=118)
        .facet(facet=alt.Facet("panel:N", sort=order, title=None), columns=4)
        .resolve_scale(x="independent", y="independent")
        .configure_view(stroke="#e4e3df")
        .configure_header(labelColor="#8d8b86", labelFontSize=12)
    )
```

## `n_neighbors`: local versus global

`n_neighbors` (default 15) is the size of the neighborhood UMAP considers for each point. Small
values focus on fine local detail, at the cost of the big picture. Large values preserve more
global structure, at the cost of detail.

```{python}
#| echo: false
grid("n_neighbors", [5, 15, 50, 200])
```

With 5 neighbors, the digits break up into many small fragments. With 200, digits that look
alike move together. Typical values are 5 to 50. polars-umap reduces `n_neighbors` to the number
of rows minus one when needed.

## `min_dist`: tight or spread out

`min_dist` (default 0.1) is the minimum distance between points in the embedding. Small values
give tight, dense clusters, which helps for clustering. Large values spread the points out, which
shows more of the structure within a cluster.

```{python}
#| echo: false
grid("min_dist", [0.0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.99])
```

`min_dist` must lie between 0 and `spread` (default 1.0), which sets the overall scale.

## `metric`

The distance metric of the input space. Use `"cosine"` for text and image embeddings, whose length
usually carries no meaning, and `"euclidean"` (the default) for most other numeric data. Also
available: `"manhattan"`, `"chebyshev"`, `"minkowski"`, `"correlation"` and `"hamming"`.

## `n_components`

The number of output dimensions. Use 2 for plots. For clustering or as input to another model,
values like 5 or 10 often preserve more structure.

## The rest

| Parameter | When to change it |
|---|---|
| `n_epochs` | Fewer is faster but less converged |
| `init` | Pass an array to start from an earlier layout |
| `layout` | `"0.5"` to match older umap-learn; see [Reproducibility](reproducibility.qmd) |
| `learning_rate` | Fine-tuning the optimization; rarely needed |
| `negative_sample_rate` | Fine-tuning the optimization; rarely needed |
| `repulsion_strength` | Fine-tuning the optimization; rarely needed |
| `local_connectivity` | How the neighbor graph is built; rarely needed |
| `set_op_mix_ratio` | How the neighbor graph is built; rarely needed |
| `a`, `b` | Override the curve from `min_dist` and `spread` |
| `disconnection_distance` | Cut edges longer than this in the neighbor graph |

See the [reference](../reference/umap.qmd) for every parameter.
